slice: VS2 - Gate Select to Hunt exploration and return

authorization.grants: VS2-PREP, then this contract, then bounded VS2 implementation, then STOP FOR OWNER REVIEW.
authorization.flow: RAISING HOME -> GATE SELECT -> HUNT LOADOUT -> HUNT FIELD -> WILD CREATURE PRESENTATION -> EXPLORE -> EXIT -> RETURN RAISING HOME
authorization.excludedNote: These are outside VS2 by Owner instruction. They are not missing features of this contract, and presentation must not imply they are one tap away.

purpose: The only surface Codex binds VS2 presentation to. Codex reads frames and raises intents; it never reads Claude internal state and never holds gameplay truth. Everything here is read-only except the named intents. This is the same seam shape as INT_RH2_RUNTIME_PRESENTATION_CONTRACT, extended to three screens.

consumerRules.note: The factory is the whole seam. If presentation needs a value that is not on a frame, that is a contract change request to Claude, not an import.

rendererSplit.dom: Gate Select and Hunt Loadout screens, the Hunt HUD, all menus, panels, toolbar and text - Codex, P1R system
rendererSplit.pixi: The Hunt playable field, terrain, props, wild creatures, the player marker and 2D VFX - Claude owns the runtime integration, Codex owns visual QA and art
rendererSplit.three: NOT USED IN VS2. Original gate_select 3D models and the ART-R4 3D baseline are Owner-approved REFERENCE material, which is not an approval to ship a 3D runtime. Bounded 3D remains a separate Owner gate.
rendererSplit.stageNote: VS2 introduces one shared Pixi stage host so that Raising and Hunt are scenes on a single Application. A second `new PIXI.Application()` would break the invariant the migration firewall enforces.

api.getFrame(): returns the current screen frame; pure read, never mutates. Publishes on DISCRETE change only - a screen change, a selection, a save.
api.subscribe(listener): listener(frame) on every discrete change; returns an unsubscribe function
api.intents: the object described under `intents` below - player actions only
api.field.getView({ viewportWidth, viewportH: continuous positional read for the field renderer: camera, visible chunks, player, wild creatures, objects, and an isBlockedTile(x, y) probe. Returns null off the Hunt field.
api.field.tick(deltaMs): relay from the one Application-owned ticker. Not a gameplay intent.

producer.twoCadences: Field motion is continuous. Republishing a frame sixty times a second would drag every DOM observer along with it, so the field renderer reads field.getView() each tick instead. Both read the same runtime; neither holds a second copy of it.
producer.note: Codex must not import championshipStandaloneApp, championshipRaisingProduction, the gate/hunt/field runtimes, any R2 module, or any catalog. This factory is the whole seam.

screens.note: One screen is active at a time. `frame.screen` names it. There is no second router: the screen stack is a bounded stack owned by the standalone application, and presentation reads its current value rather than driving navigation itself.
transitions: HUNT_FIELD -> HUNT_RESULT (exitHunt with actual inserted cards)
HUNT_RESULT -> RAISING_HOME (confirmHuntResult after successful existing save)
screens.returnLifecycle: Empty expedition returns Home. Actual on-card records enter existing HUNT_RESULT, then atomic Home/save commit. Normal return applies verified history/modifier/RNG writes once; screen navigation does not create capture ownership.
screens.raisingHomeNote: RAISING_HOME content is published by the VS1 seam, createRaisingPresentationSource. This source reports the active screen and owns the expedition screens only, so `frame.gateSelect`, `frame.huntLoadout` and `frame.huntField` are all null while Raising Home is active.

commonFrameFields.revision: integer, increments on every runtime change; use it to skip redundant repaints

save.phase: DIRTY | SAVED | RESTORED | RECOVERED | CLEAN | SAVE_FAILED

toolbar.note: Historical neutral shell is for the exploration/replay fixture. Normal Hunt uses toolState.tools through the same DOM seam; do not render both rails.
toolbar.slots: eight entries, identical in shape to the Raising toolbar frame: buttonNode, frame geometry, submenuCapacity 8, and null commandId / iconCell / label at UNKNOWN_REQUIRES_TRACE
toolbar.presentationRule: Render all eight slots as the ROM-verified shell in ROM order at ROM geometry, every slot a neutral disabled placeholder carrying its raw slot id. Do not label, icon, or activate any slot. Do not hide slots to make the row look finished. The Hunt toolbar is present on HUNT_FIELD only; GATE_SELECT and HUNT_LOADOUT have no ROM-verified toolbar mode and therefore show none.

gates.ordinal: 1-based position in the product gate list
gates.displayName: Localized display string for the recovered Gate name
gates.biomeOrdinal: 1..16. Codex binds art by ordinal: the O3-C representative catalog is Codex-owned and lives outside this repository, so the runtime does not invent ids for it.
gates.stateNote: Project initial/rank/match unlock using existing app progression. Natural rank progression is not inferred.

art.note: null means Codex has not supplied art; the runtime renders neutral geometry

gates.displayNameEvidence: ROM_VERIFIED source name with presentation localization

gateCount.source: 17-entry Gate table,16 ordinary nodes plus1 separate tutorial Grass node

affordances.note: Pointer Events only. Mouse and touch share one path. No directional input model exists.

gateSelectFrame.admission: Immutable {gateId,canConfigure,canEnter,reason,entranceFeeBits,chargeBits,walletBits,afterBits,unlockKind,unlockParameter,evidence}; no-selection has canConfigure/canEnter false and NO_GATE_SELECTED.

huntLoadoutFrame.availableEquipment: Existing Shop-owned stock grouped by recovered class
huntLoadoutFrame.entryError: Admission or candidate-construction failure; null otherwise
huntLoadoutFrame.selectionRule: No required full loadout; no normal companion selector. Carried-actor entry remains unbound.

huntFieldFrame.evidenceState: STRUCTURE_ROM_VERIFIED for world geometry and collision bounds; movement, encounter and marker semantics are UNKNOWN_REQUIRES_TRACE

tileSizePx.note: Original tile pixel size is a presentation decision at 2026 resolution; the tile COUNT is the preserved fact.

chunkSizeTiles.note: Streaming granularity only. Not an original structure claim.

world.preservationRule: The Hunt world is a large modular field traversed by a camera. 9:16 is the VIEWPORT, never the world. The field must not be flattened into one screen-sized scene, and the logical grid must stay hidden from the player - no tile lines, no coordinate readout, no grid overlay.

camera.note: Clamped inside the world. Presentation renders what this window describes and never derives its own camera.

terrain.note: Terrain reaches presentation through field.getView(), not through the discrete frame: it is camera-dependent and changes as the player walks.
terrain.isBlockedTile: (tileX, tileY) => boolean. The only terrain query, because only two collision outcomes are evidenced: attribute bit 0 set (or out of bounds) blocks, and everything else is unresolved.

kinds.note: A richer terrain taxonomy - water, forest, cliff, path - is UNKNOWN_REQUIRES_TRACE and must not be invented in either runtime or art. Codex may vary the LOOK of OPEN and BLOCKED per biome; it must not imply a third traversal rule.

terrain.unresolvedNote: Attribute bits 1 through 7 remain unresolved. The runtime treats them as traversable and reports them as unresolved rather than claiming they are safe.
terrain.hiddenGridRule: No tile lines, no coordinate readout, no grid overlay - and no per-chunk tinting either: a visible 16x16 streaming seam is still a grid the player can see.

objects.note: Object placement is part of the preserved modular-field structure. Individual original object identities are not traced, so VS2 objects are product-authored neutral placements. VS2 emits SCENERY only: BLOCKER stays declared but unused, because collision authority is the attribute grid and a second visual source of blocking would be a second authority.

wildBehaviourDeclaration.detail: No original wild-creature movement, spawn rule, aggression, flee response or encounter trigger is traced. VS2 gives wild creatures a bounded, deterministic, seeded wander inside the verified collision rule and nothing else. They do not approach the player, react to the player, flee, chase, or trigger anything.
wildBehaviourDeclaration.presentationRule: Presentation must not add reaction, alert, aggression, exclamation marks, detection cones, or capture affordances. VS3 owns Capture; suggesting it here would pre-empt an unauthorized slice.
wildBehaviourDeclaration.guard: PD-HUNT-CAPTURE: the original tether/circle capture grammar must not degrade into a single Capture button. VS2 ships no capture surface at all.
wildBehaviourDeclaration.placementNote: Wild creatures are placed in widening bands 9 to 45 tiles from the spawn, not scattered uniformly across 16,384 tiles. Uniform scattering is defensible as a model and useless as a field: the camera shows roughly 24 by 49 tiles. Neither placement is evidenced; this is the product-authored choice that makes the slice legible.

hud.note: Deliberately minimal. hunt_sub_scene carries map_marker0..23 and remain_icon0..3 with remain_time0..3 as STRUCTURAL evidence only - the node names are known, their semantics are not. VS2 renders none of them rather than guessing what 24 markers count or what 4 timers measure.

affordances.note: Inverse pointer delta pans the existing camera. Target touch selects one wild ID; unknown native tool and ownership writers remain gated.

intents.note: The only mutation entry points. Codex calls these; Codex never writes state.
intents.selectGate(gateId | null): set or clear gate selection on GATE_SELECT
intents.confirmGate(): GATE_SELECT -> HUNT_LOADOUT using the current selection; a no-op with no selection
intents.selectCompanion(creatureId | null): set or clear the companion on HUNT_LOADOUT
intents.beginHunt(): HUNT_LOADOUT -> HUNT_FIELD; a no-op until a companion is selected
intents.leaveScreen(): step one screen back: GATE_SELECT -> RAISING_HOME, HUNT_LOADOUT -> GATE_SELECT
intents.requestSave(): persist; returns the updated save block
intents.panCamera(deltaX, deltaY, viewportWidth,: Continuous world-unit camera delta with the current field viewport dimensions; no avatar move and no discrete DOM publication.
intents.selectWildAt(worldX, worldY): Select an existing wild ID using the explicitly product-authored hit radius. Does not alter HP or ownership.
intents.abortEnclosureStroke(): Discard an uncommitted diagnostic stroke. Never finish or submit it.
intents.beginEnclosureStroke / extendEnclosureSt: Legacy diagnostic intents only, not called by the player pointer. End returns TOOL_TRACE_REQUIRED and cannot create a result or collection entry.

saveAndData.authority: Unchanged. One save key, championshipModernSave:v1, one durable writer, one envelope.

vs2Writes.detail: VS2 adds no new save field. Gate selection, loadout and field position are session state, not persisted progress, because no original persistence for them is traced and the standalone envelope is deny-by-default on unknown keys.
vs2Writes.consequence: A reload during a Hunt returns the player to Raising Home with the Raising slice intact. That is the honest behaviour for a slice with no traced Hunt persistence, not a defect.

saveAndData.forbidden: Codex must not add save fields. That remains a Claude-owned contract change.

temporaryTechnicalArt.detail: Original-created neutral technical field and resident presentation for architecture proof only. O1 Gate/Hunt, O3-C and P1R are reference INPUTS, not shippable material.

forbidden: any original ROM pixel or ROM-derived binary asset
any path outside assets/production/ in a runtime declaration
any implication that temporary technical art is final production art
assetPolicy.absentArtBehaviour: Every art hook on a frame may be null. The runtime renders product-authored neutral geometry when it is, exactly as the Raising field already does. Missing art never blocks the slice, and it never authorizes Claude to invent visual production authority.

excludedFromPresentation.note: Deliberately absent. Requesting any of these is a contract violation, not a missing feature.
fields: capture affordances of any kind - VS3 owns Capture
hunt result, rewards, currency, or progression - VS3 and VS6
battle entry from the field - VS5
shop or database entry points - VS4
encounter counters, remaining-time meters, or the 24 map markers - node names are known, semantics are not
creature stat values - ROM proves the ten status fields exist; no values exist in this build
tile lines, grid overlays or coordinate readouts - the logical grid stays hidden
gate completion, ranking, star or progress indicators - no unlock rule is traced
any forensic catalog record, evidence claim, or promotion manifest field

criteria: the Hunt camera window stays inside the world at every viewport

invariants: one save key and one durable writer

implementation.screenStack: src/championship/app/championshipScreenStack.js - a bounded stack with an explicit legal-transition table. No URL, no history, no route table, no lazy loading: it is not a second router.
implementation.huntWorld: src/championship/hunt/huntWorld.js - builds a real 128x128 FieldDefinition through the existing field kernel, so the frozen contract validates every world before it can be used.
implementation.pixiStage: src/championship/presentation/championshipPixiStage.js - the one Application for the whole product. Raising and Hunt are scenes on it, and the canvas is re-parented across a screen change rather than rebuilt.
implementation.domShell: src/championship/app/vs2Screens.js - a NEUTRAL RUNTIME SHELL, not a visual production decision. DOM screen UI is Codex's lane and the P1R system is the approved standard; these screens exist so the flow is playable and testable now, and they consume only this seam - exactly what Codex will bind to when the P1R Gate/Hunt family lands.
implementation.domShellNote: The shell imports CHAMPIONSHIP_SCREENS from championshipScreenStack.js purely as a screen-id enum. A Codex replacement does not need even that: frame.screen already carries the value, so the seam remains the only required import.
